newsitem.title: USA: Senator questions earthquake disaster payments.
newsitem.headline: Senator questions earthquake disaster payments.

text.p: A senior senator Tuesday asked the Federal Emergency Management Agency to find out if federal disaster payments for the 1994 Los Angeles earthquake were made to counsel residents whose homes had no damage.

Sen. John McCain, an Arizona Republican, said he had seen news reports that disaster benefits were given to some residents to pay for counselling to help them cope with the massive damage to their neighbours' homes.

McCain asked FEMA Inspector General George Opfer to find out if the reports were true. "These charges greatly concern me. Any unauthorised or unnecessary spending that may be occurring in the agency is particulary troubling," McCain wrote Opfer.

"I would also like you to recommend what fair and appropriate steps can be taken to reclaim payments from those to whom they were improperly sent," McCain added. He said FEMA had too many outstanding disaster needs to be spending money improperly.
A FEMA spokesman in the Los Angeles area disaster relief centre said he was not aware of the payments McCain questioned.
